itemListElement.name: A Meeting Agenda Template in Word That US Teams Can Copy and Reuse in 2026

mainEntity.name: Is there a meeting agenda template in Word?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and Microsoft's own gallery names them: Bold meeting agenda, Team meeting agenda, Education meeting agenda and PTA agenda all sit under its free minutes and agenda templates. Read the columns before you commit, since the designer-led ones usually carry a topic column and nothing for time or owner.

mainEntity.name: How do I make a meeting agenda in Word?

acceptedAnswer.text: Build it once in a 4-column table, then save it as a template. Microsoft Support notes that Office drops it in the Custom Office Templates folder, so it shows up under File, then New, then Personal on any machine signed in to the same account. Macros need the .dotm format instead.

mainEntity.name: What is the best format for a meeting agenda?

acceptedAnswer.text: Goal first, then each topic with its time box, owner and the decision needed. Public bodies have a stricter bar: under California Government Code section 54954.2, a posted agenda needs a brief general description of every item, generally 20 words or fewer, and nothing off the agenda can be acted on.

mainEntity.name: How do I save an agenda as a template in Word?

acceptedAnswer.text: Go to File, then Save As, and choose Word Template (.dotx). Word opens a fresh copy every time, so the master survives. One quirk worth knowing: double-clicking the .dotx file in Finder or File Explorer also opens a new document rather than the template, which is why edits to the master must start from File, then Open.

mainEntity.name: When should I send a meeting agenda?

acceptedAnswer.text: For internal meetings, 24 hours ahead is enough, and 1 to 2 days for client or board meetings. Public agencies in California get no choice: Government Code section 54954.2 requires the agenda for a regular meeting to be posted at least 72 hours in advance, in a place the public can reach freely.

mainEntity.name: Can I use the same agenda template in Google Docs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, paste the text and table straight in. Google also ships a shortcut Word does not have. Type "@" in a Doc and pick the meeting notes building block, which pulls the title, date and guest list from the Google Calendar event.
